The Vault holds very sensitive client data, so Social Security, passport, tax ID and account numbers can be shown in full, masked to the last 4 digits, or hidden completely. That setting is made per view (Heritage Platform Weekly Sync, 1 Oct 2026) [File Deal Strategy/Product-Segmentation.md (part 6)]. Invited viewers get the masked or hidden version.

But no meeting recorded in the vault actually decided that rule for invited viewers. The file says outright that it's inferred from the meetings above [File Deal Strategy/Product-Segmentation.md (part 6)]. So "protecting sensitive data shared outside Heritage staff" is a reasonable reading, not a recorded decision.

**What the vault does record:**
- **What masking hides.** When identifiers are censored, the full date of birth is hidden too (14 Oct 2026). On asset sheets, tax IDs show only the last 4 digits (16 Sep 2026) [File Deal Strategy/Product-Segmentation.md (part 6)].
- **Who invited viewers are.** In the pilot, clients and their advisers have view-only access (Heritage Platform Weekly Sync, 2 Sep 2026) [File Technical Strategy/Use-Cases-and-Feedback.md (part 1)]. Secure access (#35) gives clients a read-only role and is in production [File Deal Strategy/Product-Segmentation.md (part 2)].
- **The downside, raised by Heritage staff.** Someone preparing a tax return may need the full number and then has to ask for it (1 Oct 2026) [File Deal Strategy/Product-Segmentation.md (part 6)].

**What's missing:** Feature-Rationale has no entry for identifier masking [File Technical Strategy/Feature-Rationale.md (part 2)]. To confirm why viewers get the masked form, and who chose that, check the Heritage Platform Weekly Sync transcript from 1 Oct 2026 and the Linear issue for secure access (#35). If it was a deliberate decision, I can draft a Feature-Rationale row for it, which would need your approval.

The files don't say Heritage found any security issue themselves. The likeliest answer is the hosting problem: the April MSA requires US-only hosting, but the database was found in Central Europe, and the DPE project moves it [File Technical Strategy/Phasing-Commercial.md (part 3)]. That file says only that it "was found", citing the Heritage, Ridgeback, Supernal Weekly Call of 5 Oct 2026. It doesn't say whether Heritage or Supernal found it.

The other security events in the vault don't fit "found by the client":
- **Malware incident, July 2026.** This was at Supernal and froze deployments for every client, Heritage included (Delivery Planning Weekly, 13 Jul 2026). Supernal told Heritage it was contained in 58 minutes and no Heritage data was affected [File Sales Strategy/Sales-Context.md (part 3)].
- **2FA lockout, 25 Oct 2026.** Turning on 2FA in production locked clients out, and it was reverted the same day [File Sales Strategy/Sales-Context.md (part 5)]. This came from a change Supernal shipped, and the file doesn't say who reported it.
- **Identifier masking.** Heritage staff pointed out that someone preparing a tax return may need a client's full number and would then have to ask for it [File Deal Strategy/Product-Segmentation.md (part 6)]. That's a complaint about how the masking works, not a security hole.

Security-and-Compliance should have the answer. It's meant to log every incident and its fix, but it only has headings, including "Roger's assessment and incident history" [File Technical Strategy/Security-and-Compliance.md]. Roger Lee promised a written security assessment on 28 Oct, to come in 1 to 2 weeks, and no Linear issue was found for it [File Delivery Strategy/Weekly.md (part 2)].

To confirm who found the Central Europe database, check the Fathom/Granola recording of the 5 Oct 2026 weekly call. Roger's questions-and-answers on the 28 Oct Heritage Platform Weekly Sync may also cover it.
